from.place: Integral exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient-adjunction and inverse-limit calculation: auxiliary simplicial localization mapping-space comparison; Dwyer–Kan Lemma 5.7, via the two-sided Grothendieck construction of Definitions 10.1–10.2 and Propositions 10.4–10.5.

title: Homotopy invariance of two-sided Grothendieck constructions over simplicial bases
statement:
Use small simplicial categories with constant object set and weak homotopy equivalences of simplicial sets as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], ordinary categories and their nerves as in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus], and bisimplicial diagonals as in [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence]. For a simplicial diagram of small categories $E_\bullet$, write $\mathsf N(E)_n=N_n(E_n)$, with both simplicial operators applied together; its object sets need not be constant. Fix a small set $O$ and a small simplicial category $V$ on $O$, and let $V_n$ be its ordinary category of degree-$n$ arrows. A covariant transfunctor $G$ on $V$ consists of functors $G_n:V_n\to\mathrm{Cat}$ and, for every $t:[n]\to[m]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, natural transformations $G_t:G_n\Rightarrow G_m V_t$. They satisfy $G_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $G_{st}=(G_s V_t)G_t$ for composable $t,s$. A contravariant transfunctor $F$ is the same data on $V^{\mathrm{op}}$. Values lie in small categories in a fixed larger universe. A transformation of transfunctors is a family of natural transformations in each degree commuting with all these structure transformations. For $z\in O$, the categories $F_n(z)$ and the functors $F_t(z)$ form a simplicial diagram $F(z)$; likewise for $G(z)$.

Define the simplicial diagram of categories $F\otimes_VG$ degreewise as follows. Objects in degree $n$ are triples $(a,z,b)$, where $a\in F_n(z)$ and $b\in G_n(z)$. A morphism $(a,z,b)\to(a',z',b')$ consists of $h:z\to z'$ in $V_n$, $u:a\to F_n(h)a'$ in $F_n(z)$, and $v:G_n(h)b\to b'$ in $G_n(z')$. For a following morphism $(h',u',v')$, composition has components $h'h$, $F_n(h)(u')u$, and $v'G_n(h')(v)$; identities are identities in all three components. The operator $t:[n]\to[m]$ sends $(a,z,b)$ to $(F_t(z)a,z,G_t(z)b)$ and $(h,u,v)$, with $h:z\to z\prime$, to $(V_t h,F_t(z)(u),G_t(z\prime)(v))$. The required fiber-arrow targets and sources are identified by the naturality equalities $F_t(z)F_n(h)=F_m(V_t h)F_t(z\prime)$ and $G_t(z\prime)G_n(h)=G_m(V_t h)G_t(z)$. For a simplicial functor $H:V'\to V$ fixing the same object set $O$, define the pulled-back transfunctor $(FH)_n=F_n H_n^{\mathrm{op}}$ and similarly $GH$.

Let $V'$ also be a small simplicial category on $O$, let $H:V'\to V$ fix objects, and let $F',G'$ be contravariant and covariant transfunctors on $V'$. Suppose there are transformations $\alpha:F'\Rightarrow FH$ and $\beta:G'\Rightarrow GH$. Assume that $V'(z,z')\to V(z,z')$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $z,z'$, and that $\mathsf N(F'(z))\to\mathsf N(F(z))$ and $\mathsf N(G'(z))\to\mathsf N(G(z))$ induced by $\alpha,\beta$ are weak homotopy equivalences for every $z$. Then the induced map
$$\mathsf N(F'\otimes_{V'}G')\longrightarrow\mathsf N(F\otimes_VG)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The inducing functor sends $(a,z,b)$ to $(\alpha(a),z,\beta(b))$, uses $H$ on base arrows, and uses $\alpha,\beta$ on fiber arrows.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Definitions 9.1 and 10.1–10.2, Propositions 10.4–10.5 and their proof 10.6, printed pp.31,33–34 (PDF pp.15,17–18). The combined comparison factors through the pullback transfunctors. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: First establish the product and coproduct facts used below. The realization of a coproduct of simplicial sets is the disjoint union of their realizations: every relation in the realization quotient retains its summand index. Path components and based homotopy groups are computed within one summand (a sphere or a path, being connected, stays there). Consequently a coproduct over a fixed small set of weak homotopy equivalences is a weak homotopy equivalence, also for the empty set. If $f:X\to X'$ is a weak homotopy equivalence and $K$ any simplicial set, apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to $X_p\times K_q\to X'_p\times K_q$. For each $q$ this is the coproduct of copies of $f$ indexed by $K_q$; the exchanged-direction clause makes its diagonal $f\times1_K$ a weak homotopy equivalence. Factor $f\times g$ as $(1\times g)(f\times1)$, interchange factors for the second map, and use composition of weak equivalences in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Induction proves preservation by all finite products, including the empty product, a point.

source.place: Proof 10.6(ii), factorwise weak-equivalence argument; product preservation expanded using the diagonal criterion.

proof.text:
For each $n$, apply the explicitly defined trisimplicial bar of [lem-coef-ordinary-two-sided-bar-comparison] to the ordinary category $V_n$ and functors $F_n,G_n$. Denote the resulting four-index set by
$$T_{n,i,k,j}=\coprod_{z_0\xrightarrow{h_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{h_k}z_k\text{ in }V_n} N_iF_n(z_k)\times N_jG_n(z_0).$$
The three bar operators are those in the cited statement. The remaining operator $t:[n]\to[m]$ applies $V_t$ to the base chain, $F_t(z_k)$ to the $F$-nerve simplex and $G_t(z_0)$ to the $G$-nerve simplex. These commute with $i,j$ operators since they are functors. They commute with internal $k$ faces and degeneracies since $V_t$ preserves composition and identities. At $d_0$, the required equality is $G_t(z_1)G_n(h_1)=G_m(V_th_1)G_t(z_0)$; at $d_k$ it is $F_t(z_{k-1})F_n(h_k)=F_m(V_th_k)F_t(z_k)$. These are exactly the transfunctor naturality equations. The identity and composition equations on transfunctors prove the $n$ simplicial identities. Explicitly, $T'_{n,i,k,j}$ is the coproduct over chains $z_0\xrightarrow{h'_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{h'_k}z_k$ in $V'_n$ of $N_iF'_n(z_k)\times N_jG'_n(z_0)$, with endpoint faces applying $G'_n(h'_1)$ and $F'_n(h'_k)$ and $n$ operators applying $V'_t,F'_t,G'_t$. The preceding endpoint equations hold with all data primed by the transfunctor hypotheses on $F',G'$. The map $T'\to T$ takes this summand to the chain $(H_nh'_1,\ldots,H_nh'_k)$ and applies $N_i\alpha_n(z_k)$ and $N_j\beta_n(z_0)$ to the factors. For $h':z\to z'$, its endpoint-face identities are
$$\beta_n(z')G'_n(h')=G_n(H_nh')\beta_n(z),\qquad \alpha_n(z)F'_n(h')=F_n(H_nh')\alpha_n(z').$$
Its $n$-operator identities are $V_tH_n=H_mV'_t$, $F_t(z)\alpha_n(z)=\alpha_m(z)F'_t(z)$ and $G_t(z)\beta_n(z)=\beta_m(z)G'_t(z)$. These follow respectively from the simplicial-functor hypothesis and the definition of transformations of transfunctors. Functoriality handles the nerve operators, internal faces and degeneracies. Thus the displayed map commutes with all four directions.

source.place: Definitions 10.1–10.2 and proof 10.6, definition of the four-simplicial set; endpoint operator checks expanded.

proof.text: Set $R_{n,r}=T_{n,r,r,r}$ and $Q_{n,r}=N_r((F\otimes_VG)_n)$. In each fixed $n$, the ordinary comparison [lem-coef-ordinary-two-sided-bar-comparison] gives its fixed-shape natural zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences from $R_{n,\bullet}$ to $Q_{n,\bullet}$. Its naturality under reindexing functors and natural transformations applies to $(V_t,F_t,G_t)$, so all intermediate sets and arrows form bisimplicial sets and maps in $(n,r)$. It also applies to $(H_n,\alpha_n,\beta_n)$, so the primed and unprimed zigzags form a strictly commuting ladder. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] separately to each zigzag arrow: it is a weak equivalence for every fixed $n$, hence also after taking $(n,r)=(r,r)$. We obtain natural zigzags of weak homotopy equivalences between $\operatorname{diag}T$ and $\mathsf N(F\otimes_VG)$ and between $\operatorname{diag}T'$ and $\mathsf N(F'\otimes_{V'}G')$, in a commuting ladder. Here the identification of $Q$ uses the identical three-component object, arrow and composition formulas; the object set of this simplicial diagram of categories need not be constant.

source.place: Proposition 9.5 and proof 10.6(i): apply the ordinary comparison degreewise, then the diagonal theorem.

proof.text:
Take instead the partial diagonal $D_{r,k}=T_{r,r,k,r}$. Because $O$ is constant, for each fixed $k$ its $r$-simplicial set is exactly
$$D_{\bullet,k}=\coprod_{(z_0,\ldots,z_k)\in O^{k+1}}\mathsf N(F(z_k))\times\Bigl(\prod_{a=1}^k V(z_{a-1},z_a)\Bigr)\times\mathsf N(G(z_0)).$$
Indeed an $r$-simplex is an $r$-nerve simplex in each endpoint fiber and an independent degree-$r$ base arrow between each consecutive pair of the fixed objects; every such tuple is a composable base chain. Applying an $r$ operator changes all those components simultaneously and retains the object tuple. This proves an isomorphism of simplicial sets, rather than identifying it with $Q_{\bullet,k}$. For the primed bar the same formula has primes throughout. As $H$ fixes $O$, the map $D'_{\bullet,k}\to D_{\bullet,k}$ retains the same summand index, uses $H$ on each mapping simplicial set, and uses the assumed diagonal-nerve maps of $\alpha,\beta$ on the two fiber factors. No degreewise weak equivalence of $NF'_n(z)\to NF_n(z)$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Proof 10.6(ii), partial diagonal in indices (r,r,k,r), with the source chain indexed in forward order.

proof.text: For every fixed $k$ all factors of the map in Step 4 are weak homotopy equivalences by the hypotheses: $\mathsf N(F'(z_k))\to\mathsf N(F(z_k))$, $V'(z_{a-1},z_a)\to V(z_{a-1},z_a)$ for each $a$, and $\mathsf N(G'(z_0))\to\mathsf N(G(z_0))$. Step 1 makes their finite products and the coproduct over $O^{k+1}$ weak homotopy equivalences, so $D'_{\bullet,k}\to D_{\bullet,k}$ is one for each $k$. The exchanged-direction assertion of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] gives $\operatorname{diag}D'\to\operatorname{diag}D$ a weak homotopy equivalence. Both diagonals are the full fourfold diagonals: their degree $r$ sets are $T'_{r,r,r,r}$ and $T_{r,r,r,r}$ with the same simultaneous operators. Hence the map $\operatorname{diag}T'\to\operatorname{diag}T$ in the ladder of Step 3 is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proof 10.6(ii), product/coproduct comparison followed by the final diagonal; proves 10.4 and 10.5 simultaneously.

proof.text: Transfer this weak equivalence through the finite commuting ladder of Step 3. For any horizontal arrow $a:A\to B$ in that ladder, write the corresponding primed arrow as $a':A'\to B'$ and the vertical maps as $f_A,f_B$. The square says $f_Ba'=af_A$. Since $a,a'$ are weak homotopy equivalences, two-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] proves that $f_A$ is a weak equivalence if and only if $f_B$ is; this works for horizontal arrows oriented either way. Beginning at the bar end (Step 5) and iterating gives the assertion at the Grothendieck-nerve end. The naturality clause of [lem-coef-ordinary-two-sided-bar-comparison] identifies that vertical map as the nerve of the degreewise functor applying $(\alpha,H,\beta)$, so its diagonal sends exactly the stated objects and fiber/base arrows to their specified images. Thus it is the required map. All coproducts are small in the fixed larger universe. For $O=\varnothing$ both sides are empty; empty endpoint fibers give empty summands; $k=0$ has the empty product of base factors and the two stated fiber factors; terminal fibers give the usual base nerve. These cases require no fibrancy or nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Proof 10.6, naturality and two-of-three concluding the combined coefficient and base comparison.

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged. Read DK Sections 9–10 online. Added one ordinary two-sided bar/Grothendieck nerve comparison (DK 9.5), stated only with naturality under arbitrary reindexing and transformations. Constructed the four-simplicial bar, applied that comparison in each base degree, identified the correct partial diagonal as fixed-index coproducts of products, proved factorwise weak invariance and transferred the actual comparison map through a natural commuting ladder. Corrected the draft conflation of the Grothendieck nerve with its bar model. No Mathlib leaf or project attachment.
